text.p: Italian bonds and futures ended the year on a bullish note with the March Btp contract on LIFFE touching a new record high in a market buoyed by hopes of an end to the long-running Italian metalworkers' pay dispute and a resulting cut in Bank of Italy key interest rates, traders said.

The market ignored weaker bunds and although a thin Italian bond market did relatively little, the March Btp future traded in London hit a new peak at 130.10 on a late buying spree, beating a previous high of 129.37 set on December 5.
Italian and U.K. markets are closed on Wednesday for New Year's Day and reopen on Thursday.
